author: Claude Opus 5.5 (engineering lead) with Claude Sonnet 5.5 (cand-a v2 implementation agent)
summary: Hexagonal-prism tumbler, version 2: one rigid hexagonal body (circumradius 25.5 mm) that rolls over its hexagon edges, driven by an internal lift ring with one lobe (geared from a 6 mm gearmotor); axial couplers on the two end faces: a fixed hex peg on the head, and a tail receiver with roll-in channel, yaw turntable, dead-centre toggle keeper and SMA pulse release. BLE only, no power transfer.

assembly_access.statement: Walls and end plates are separate PA12 parts joined by two PA12 axial posts and four M1.6 screws (screw positions are a lumped stand-in). Each wall half (head and tail) is a separate part so the lift ring can be dropped into the girdle slot between them. The cell, controller and boards load as a stack along the axis with one end plate removed; the head peg installs from the head end plate and the tail receiver cap halves, yaw puck and keeper install from the tail end. No assembly sequence has been verified, and the gear train, yaw worm and SMA routing are not shown to be assemblable.

coupler_sites.mount: datum on the head peg axis where a neighbour's tail face sits when docked (gap g = 8 mm from the head end face at y = 14 mm, 5 mm peg engagement)
tail receiver on end plate b (tail face)

retention.mechanism: The head peg's annular groove (dia 3.0 x 1.6 wide) is closed by a 0.8 mm 304 keeper tongue driven by a two-link dead-centre toggle in the tail yaw puck. In the closed state the toggle links lie on or just past dead centre, biased closed by a Lee LC 014A 01 S spring at 0.2 mm installed compression (0.33 N), so axial pull on the peg bears on the tongue and the puck wall and its load line passes through the link pins and cannot back-drive the toggle. Torsion about the axis is carried by the hex peg in the half-hex cup. Nothing is powered to hold. Closing is passive: the arriving peg trips the toggle past centre (trip energy fraction UNRESOLVED).

release.means: A one-second pulse in the unit's own 0.004 in Flexinol wire pulls the toggle knee 0.3 mm past dead centre; the spring then snaps the keeper open and it stays open unpowered. Needs 0.82 N at the knee against 1.40 N recommended pull (1.7x) and 0.3 mm against 0.88 mm stroke at 4% strain. It acts only on this unit's own receiver and needs no help from the neighbour, which can also roll away about the same edge. Heat, cycle life and the pulse current limit are UNRESOLVED.

alignment.description: Roll-in channel: two circular-arc slots in the tail cap halves, radius 25.5 mm, centred on the two bottom vertices, from the mid-height vertices to the face centre, 5.4 mm wide, 5.5 mm deep, 45 deg x 1.5 mm flared mouths.
alignment.justification: When unit B rolls one step about its leading bottom edge, a neighbour's peg lying on the common axis moves in B's frame along exactly this arc, keeps its direction (parallel to y) and turns 60 deg about its own axis (hex symmetry), so B can roll into a docked pose using its own lift drive and gravity. Slot width 5.4 mm against the 4.619 mm across-corner peg gives 0.39 mm per side, plus 1.5 mm of flare: lateral +-1.89 mm at the mouth, height +-0.39 mm, heading +-atan(0.39/5) = +-4.5 deg, roll any multiple of 60 deg. Axial error must be inside the keeper lane (+-0.8 mm). These are nominal geometric estimates; the capture window is not claimed (CPL-006) and SLS tolerance is UNRESOLVED. No magnet and no cone.

alignment.description: Tongue V-notch seating: the keeper tongue has a V-notch (3.1 mm for the 3.0 mm groove, 6.0 mm mouth, 30 deg half-angle) that centres the peg in the half-hex cup as the toggle closes.
alignment.justification: The notch mouth (6.0 - 3.1)/2 = +-1.45 mm laterally pulls the peg into the cup as the tongue closes; the toggle snap force (0.33 N to 0.82 N) must exceed the head-end friction of the other unit, mu W/2 (0.18 N at mu = 1 for the declared 36.6 g mass), a margin of 1.9x at the low end of the spring range, UNRESOLVED dynamically. The tongue (0.8 mm) enters the 1.6 mm groove with 0.4 x 45 deg chamfers. Passive geometry and a spring only.

alignment.description: Hex peg in half-hex cup with 0.5 x 45 deg tip chamfer on the peg.
alignment.justification: The hexagonal peg (4.0 mm across flats) has six equivalent roll positions every 60 deg and is guided into the cup by its 0.5 mm chamfer; the flats carry torsion. No attractive force acts: a unit that is not driven does not self-dock.

limitations: Roll-in docking was checked on paper only; the dynamics (impact, whether the ring-driven roll closes the trip), the trip energy fraction and the capture window are UNRESOLVED and belong to later gates.
No steering or axial locomotion is provided: the body rolls only perpendicular to its axis.

Yaw bending works only while the chain rests on a face with a vertical yaw axis. The worm self-locks only if the worm/sector friction coefficient is at least 0.125 (UNRESOLVED), so a bend angle is treated as actively maintained.

Many masses are upper bounds from solid volumes (walls, end plates, caps, puck, peg, lobe); the placement of the screws and the harness is a lumped stand-in; the peg root box, keeper-in-puck volume and meshing gears are box approximations.

Gear teeth are integer: ring 133 T pitch r 19.95 and pinion 14 T pitch r 2.1 (module 0.3, centre distance 17.85); spurs 41 T and 16 T at module 0.2 (centre distance 5.70); yaw worm 1 start into 27 teeth per turn at module 0.3. Tooth strength, backlash, profile and contact ratio are not assessed.
SLS PA12 dimensional tolerance is not cited; all fit and window numbers are nominal. PA12 strength is not assessed beyond the coupler bearing checks; heat is not assessed.
The release SMA peak is computed at the full 3.7 V (1.336 A); the datasheet gives about 200 mA for a 1 s pulse, so a real driver would limit the current and the peak is a conservative bound.
The Precision Microdrives 206-109 datasheet is headed as a sampling/target specification; the motors run from 3.7 V by PWM limited to 3.0 V effective, a control constraint.

The QT Py regulator is rated 600 mA peak; the 2220 mW term is a bound; later board revisions may use a different regulator. The board has no LiPo charger, and regulator dropout limits use near the end of charge.

Vendor product pages (Grepow, Adafruit, Pololu) are classed datasheet because the schema allows only datasheet or publication. Cited values were read on 2026-11-06 and are checked by sampling at the gate record.
Spring wire (ASTM A313) and A2 screws are costed at 304 density (assumption).
Only two axial couplers are declared; no lateral side-face couplers, no branching or lattices. No through-coupler data or power contacts; power transfer is not provided.
